subject: 78EEE69EFBD4EAB9E0EF7A643386FA7E
introduction: Bahá’u’lláh and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá often retell how Muhammad was received: the nobles and divines of Mecca rejected Him, a shepherd and a Persian stranger believed, He was stoned and driven out, called madman and sorcerer; Jews and Christians who awaited a prophet did not recognize Him; and Western writers repeated slanders for centuries. The purpose is partly to defend Muhammad to Christians and partly to hold up a mirror to Muslims who rejected the Báb. The Qur’an tells the same story about every messenger, “a wizard or a madman!”, and the Gospels about Jesus: the prophet without honour at home, Jerusalem that kills the prophets, the things hidden from the wise. Carlyle’s lecture of 1840 was the first major defence of Muhammad in English and agrees with readings 36 to 38. The Christian grounds for refusing him are given in their own words, “no man cometh unto the Father, but by me” and “the faith once delivered”, and Dante’s placing of Muhammad in hell stands for the inherited picture the readings contest.
questions: The readings say the learned rejected and the simple believed, in every age. Why might learning make recognition harder?
“We believe in Christ and He is sufficient.” State the Christian objection fairly, and then the readings’ reply.
Carlyle called the lies about Muhammad “disgraceful to ourselves only”. What false pictures of another religion have you inherited, and from where?
The guide holds up Muhammad’s rejection as a mirror for Muslims who rejected the Báb. Who else is meant to look in it?
Is persecution evidence of truth? What does Jesus’s “woe unto you, when all men shall speak well of you” establish, and what does it not?

outside.why: Those who loved the Light believed; those who loved the lantern did not. The light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.
The noble and the divines turned away; a shepherd believed. Not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble, are called.
By what proof did you believe in Muhammad, and by what do you turn from the one who came after? Had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me.
Thirteen years of persecution in Mecca. They wandered in deserts, and in mountains, and in dens and caves of the earth.
They sought to kill the Messenger, and He left for Medina. Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt.
He called people to unity, and they did what made the stones of Mecca weep. O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee.
They broke His tooth and stoned His heels till the blood ran. He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief.
A law against converts to the religion of “the sorcerer”. The Qur’an: there came no messenger unto those before them but they said: a wizard or a madman!
The same charge against Jesus: this fellow doth not cast out devils, but by Beelzebub the prince of the devils.
No one was so afflicted. Messengers indeed have been denied before thee, and they were patient under the denial and the persecution till Our succour reached them.
Salmán came from Persia and believed; His own relatives rose against Him. A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country, and in his own house.
Abú Jahl, called “Father of Wisdom”, rejected Him. Thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes.
Jews and Christians who were expecting a prophet turned away when He came. Search the scriptures; they are they which testify of me. And ye will not come to me.
The divines were shut out while the shepherd attained. The first told of another birth were shepherds abiding in the field.
All united to shed His blood; afterwards His Cause prevailed. If it be of God, ye cannot overthrow it.
Those who broke the earlier covenant opposed Him. Which of the prophets have not your fathers persecuted?
He came with proof, and they clung to what they had. We found our fathers following a religion, and we are following their footprints.
“Thou art but a madman.” Ah, the anguish for the bondmen! Never came there unto them a messenger but they did mock him!
They objected, each with his own phrase. Those who disbelieve say: this is naught else than fables of the men of old.

Much that is written about Muhammad in the West is fabrication. Carlyle said so to a London audience in 1840: the lies, which well-meaning zeal has heaped round this man, are disgraceful to ourselves only.
A question from those among whom He has been spoken of with contempt. Carlyle’s own estimate: a silent great soul; he was one of those who cannot but be in earnest.
European and American historians have mostly repeated slander. He that is first in his own cause seemeth just; but his neighbour cometh and searcheth him.

A thousand books were written against Christ, too. Woe unto you, when all men shall speak well of you! for so did their fathers to the false prophets. Is being attacked evidence for a prophet? What else must be shown?
Each community denies the next one’s miracles. An evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign.
No Christian praises Islam and no Jew has a good word for Christ. Swift: we have just enough religion to make us hate, but not enough to make us love one another.

“We believe in Christ and He is sufficient; why should we accept Muhammad?” The Christian objection rests on words like these: I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me. How do the readings understand such claims to finality (see 45 and 54)?

Christians thought God’s purpose was completed in Christ. Jude speaks of the faith which was once delivered unto the saints. Every religion in the guide makes this move against its successor. What would it take to break the pattern?
Muhammad came according to the Gospels, read spiritually. Reading 50 cites this passage: Art thou that prophet? And he answered, No.
The promise behind “that prophet”: the Lord thy God will raise up unto thee a Prophet from the midst of thee, of thy brethren, like unto me.
The splitting of the moon has more than its outward meaning. The Qur’an on demands for wonders: naught hindereth Us from sending portents save that the folk of old denied them.

Jesus counselled the people of the Gospel to await the one to come. If I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you. Muslims have read this of Muhammad.
Jewish divines turned from Jesus, and Christian ones from Muhammad. Ye build the sepulchres of the prophets, and your fathers killed them.
The Pharisees said He had broken the Sabbath and defied Moses. The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath.
What the clergy of each religion did in turn. They be blind leaders of the blind.
“Say to the learned: Fear God.” Thou therefore which teachest another, teachest thou not thyself?
In Islam conflict arose over names: imam, successor, chief. Every one of you saith, I am of Paul; and I of Apollos; and I of Cephas. Is Christ divided?
Muslims thought themselves supreme for twelve hundred years. If the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted?

Dante, the greatest poet of Christendom, put Muhammad among the sowers of schism in the hell over whose gate he wrote: all hope abandon, ye who enter in. These readings were written to people raised on that picture. What does it take to unlearn an inherited contempt?

Princes and divines summoned without exception. The Gospel also counsels reserve: neither cast ye your pearls before swine. Why do the Prophets, on these readings’ account, address those most likely to reject them?
